title: Stay in Flow From Document Intake to Final Deliverable
format_note: One continuous screen recording of a legal workflow (prompt, review table, drafted memo, export) between a dark logo card and a dark tagline card.
one_thing: A lawyer goes from one prompt to an exported, tracked-changes memo without leaving Harvey, shown as an uncut real-UI recording with one camera.

transcript.voice_style: No voice. Whisper returned only a repeated 'The' on music, so it was discarded; the YouTube video has no caption track.
transcript.script_shape: Everything is carried by the user's typed prompt, the assistant's reply text and four title cards: 'Move Faster with Legal Agents', 'Stay in the Flow from Start to Finish', 'AI Tailored for Law', Harvey.

structure.frame0: Near-black card with the white serif wordmark 'Harvey' centred (f0001.jpg), 59 px tall. Brand only, no product; mean luminance 0.059 and 95% blank cells per metrics frame0.
structure.first_3s: Wordmark fades to 1.27 s, hard cut to white card 'Move Faster with Legal Agents' (strips/window-01-1.233s.jpg), then the Harvey home screen with the prompt box appears by t=2-4 s.

beats.what: Dark card, Harvey wordmark fading out.
White card: Move Faster with Legal Agents.
Harvey home: prompt typed, Project Sandbar attached, cursor presses send.
Chat reply recommends a review table; proposed table appears; cursor reaches 'Yes, build a Review table'.
Workspace scales up: chat left, 47-row review table right; camera pushes in on rows.
Second prompt drafts a memo; assistant reasoning steps stream on a full-screen text view.
Memo opens with 35 tracked changes; edits resolve to a clean draft.
Camera zooms to Export; cursor lands on it.
White card: Stay in the Flow from Start to Finish.
Dark card: AI Tailored for Law, Harvey wordmark below.

hero_moment.what: The workspace pops from a tiny thumbnail to full size with the 47-row review table filling the right half (strips/window-08-18s.jpg, 18.0-18.97 s).

ending.what: Tagline on dark from 46.97 s, wordmark added by 48 s (f0025.jpg), held to 51 s. No URL or button.

rhythm.how_change_is_paced: One shot runs 45.67 s (89.5% of runtime). Change comes from typing, cursor moves, scale-ups and camera pushes inside it; only hard cuts are at 1.3 s and 46.97 s. No bursts.

look.ground: White (84.6% of sampled frames light) for the whole product section; near-black #0f100c-like cards for open and close. Luma 222.8, saturation 0.019.
look.accent_use: No brand accent. The only strong colour is the red tracked-change text in the memo (f0017.jpg) and tiny blue/red source icons.
look.type: Serif display (Harvey wordmark and titles, one size per card) over a grotesque UI sans. Titles sentence-case, centred, single line, no accent word.
look.depth: Flat. UI sits on a faint card with a hairline shadow on white; no parallax, 3D or backgrounds.

product_ui.camera_on_ui: Scale-up from thumbnail at 18 s, slow push and pan on the table 20-24 s, zoom into the top-right corner to Export at 41-43 s. Typing and cursor stay in view.
product_ui.notes: Home and reply views are large (prompt text about 14 px at 720p, reply type 19 px). Workspace views at t=18, 32-40 s show 5-7 px table and memo text; legible only in the pushed-in frames f0011-f0013 and f0022.

motion.text_entry: Title cards switch by hard cut or fade-in; UI text types character by character (f0003 'contracts fro' to f0004) and streams word by word in the reply (strips/window-04-9.866s.jpg).
motion.ui_motion: Panels reflow: prompt box rises as the file chip appears; reply collapses into a smaller thread; 'Yes, build a Review table' pill isolated on white at 16 s; redlines resolve into clean text 34-38 s.
motion.camera: Virtual camera pushes in and out on the recorded UI: 4 s idle, then zoom to full-width text at 10 s, thumbnail-to-full at 18 s, push at 20-24 s, zoom to Export at 41-43 s.
motion.eases: Smooth settles on scale-ups (strips/window-08-18s.jpg); text arrival is linear typing. Exact easing not measured.

transitions.cause: Logo card to title card, and title card to closing card; no on-screen cause.
Cursor press on send or 'Yes, build' triggers the next view scaling up.
Product event: reply completes, memo opens, edits accepted.
Title card to white UI and white UI to white title card.

on_screen_lines.text: Extract each of the key terms and run a comprehensive change of control analysis over each of the attached material contracts from the data room.
This query would work best with a review table. It lets you run multiple questions across several documents...
Draft the Material Contracts section of my deal HVY Services, Inc. - LPS Inc. - Diligence Memo.docx based only on the provisions and insights...
Stay in the Flow from Start to Finish

copy.holds_vs_reading_rule: Title cards: 'Move Faster with Legal Agents' holds about 0.7 s against the 2.0 s the rule asks; the closing line holds 4.0 s. UI prose is shown to be seen, not read; the long reply holds about 3.5 s.

sound.music: Sustained music with no steady beat (beats confidence 0.033, bpm null). Describe tags: music 0.727, keyboard_musical 0.478, synthesizer 0.359; gong 0.259 and organ 0.258 are weaker. Sections change at 9.5, 19, 28.5, 37.5, 47 s.
sound.sfx: No sound effects identified; strong onsets at 17.25 s (0.92) and 36.485 s (1.0) are the largest, with no matching picture event at 36.5 s.
sound.vo_music_balance: No voice. Music only; sustain 0.97, voiced 0.012.
sound.energy_arc: Flat: LRA 2.1 LU, short-term max -12.9 LUFS; no silence span and no built climax.
sound.sync_to_picture: Cuts are not locked to the sound: cuts_on_strong_onset_share 0.0 against chance_share 0.066 (2 cuts).

good.observation: One uncut recording shows the whole job. A reader sees intake, analysis, drafting and export as one thread, which is the claim in the title.
The camera moves to the thing that matters: thumbnail scale-up on the table, then a push to the Export button, so the final action is unmistakable.
Real product UI with a real cursor and typed text, plausible legal content (Project Sandbar, 47 files, 35 tracked changes) makes it credible.
Strong restraint: white ground, one serif for titles, no accent colour, centred single-line titles at 7-9% height; it reads as the brand.
Isolated pill 'Yes, build a Review table' on empty white gives the click a clean beat before the big reveal.
Loudness lands on spec for social: -14.4 LUFS integrated, -1.8 dBTP.

weak.observation: Workspace views are too small for a phone: table and memo text is about 5-7 px tall at 720p across 18-40 s, so the content that proves the product cannot be read.
Opening title 'Move Faster with Legal Agents' holds about 0.7 s before the UI replaces it, too short to read five words.
Static for long stretches: 40% of sampled intervals static, one run of 6 s ending at 8 s; 32-40 s shows small edits on an unchanged page.
Music has no pulse and no peak, and the two cuts and the hero scale-up at 18 s are not on its strongest onsets.
Ends on a tagline and wordmark with no action line or URL.

rule_candidates.rule: A walkthrough can run as one uncut shot for 85-90% of the film if the camera moves (scale-up, push, zoom) every 3-6 s; hard cuts only join title cards to the product.
rule_candidates.evidence: 89.5% one shot; 2 cuts at 1.3 and 46.97 s; camera moves at 10, 18, 20-24, 41 s

rule_candidates.rule: When the product is a dense UI, zoom until working text is at least 12 px at 720p; show the full workspace under 2 s as an establishing view.
rule_candidates.evidence: workspace text 5-7 px at 18-40 s; pushed-in f0022 about 12-16 px

rule_candidates.rule: Open on a brand card (wordmark on near-black) when the next shot is a clearly branded, light product screen; the wordmark must be 7-9% of frame height and gone by 1.3 s.
Isolate a decisive click: show the button label alone on an empty ground for about 1.5 s, then scale the result into the frame.
Close with a dark title card of 4 s and a smaller wordmark added about 1 s later; swap light for dark at the cut so the end reads as an end.
rule_candidates.evidence: cut at 46.97 s; f0024-f0026; logo hold 3 s

rule_candidates.rule: Hold a title line at least 0.5 s plus 0.3 s a word; five words need 2.0 s, yet the opener gets about 0.7 s.
Show product state changes as the transitions (reply completes, memo opens, redlines accepted) instead of added effects; 6 or more cause-driven changes carry a 51 s film.
Music-only film may run without beats or a climax, but then give the hero scale-up a sound hit within 0.1 s; here the 17.25 s onset precedes the 18.0 s scale-up by 0.75 s.
rule_candidates.evidence: onsets 17.25 s strength 0.92; cut share 0.0 vs chance 0.066

unchecked: Easing curves and exact durations of scale-ups were read from strips, not measured.
Titles at 2.0 s and 43.8 s were not opened at native rate; hold times are estimates.
Sound read from tags only; instrument names are tag scores, not heard.
Whether the 36.5 s peak matches any on-screen event was not verified.
